newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans to keep medical tabs on rapists.
newsitem.headline: France plans to keep medical tabs on rapists.

text.p: The French cabinet on Wednesday approved a draft bill to increase protection of children against sex crimes by keeping sex offenders under medical supervision after they are released from prison.
The bill was drafted following Belgium's paedophile kidnap and murder scandal as well as rapes and murders of children in France that have shocked public opinion.

It also aims to fight sexual tourism by allowing prosecution in France of nationals and residents of France suspected of committing sex offences abroad. Tour operators offering sex trips could face charges of criminal conspiracy.

A major goal of the plan is to try to prevent sex criminals from repeating their offences by keeping them under medical supervision for up to 10 years after they are released from jail. They could be sent back to prison for up to four years for breaking the supervision rules.
The bill is expected to go before parliament in the spring and take effect in a year's time.

According to statistics, up to 20 percent of rapists and 25 percent of paedophiles become repeat offenders after being released from prison. Experts say medical surveillance could cut the rate of recidivism by half.
Statistics also show that sex crimes in France have increased by 40 percent over the past 10 years. Some 4,600 rapists were jailed last year, 2,800 of them for abuse of minors.
The bill says convicted paedophiles could be banned from jobs involving regular contact with children and from visiting places popular with minors.
Possession of pornographic pictures of children would become an offence. Present laws punish only the distribution of such pictures.
The law would also ban sex shops from the vicinity of schools.
